methodology: Articles sourced from Virginia-specific RSS feeds and Google News RSS, filtered for AI/technology/workforce relevance, then assessed by Claude against the scenario framework. Each article is tagged with the region it most affects and the scenario it signals toward.

signals.title: TAYLOR: AI data centers increase Virginia’s urban-rural divide - The Cavalier Daily
signals.signal_reading: Commentary directly naming the urban-rural divide around AI data centers suggests infrastructure investment is concentrating economic benefits in metros while externalizing energy costs to rural areas without distributing capability or workforce development.

signals.title: ‘Shaping our future’: Company powering AI data centers invests $50+ million in Henrico, adding 200 jobs - WWBT
signals.signal_reading: A $50M+ investment adding 200 jobs in Henrico's AI data center infrastructure strengthens Richmond's position as a concentrated tech hub, but focuses on capital-intensive infrastructure rather than distributed AI literacy or peer learning networks.

signals.title: AI pressure grows on Richmond's young workforce - Axios
signals.signal_reading: Pressure on Richmond's young workforce to adopt AI tools signals broad but potentially shallow platform-driven adoption—workers consuming AI applications rather than building deep technical capability or algorithmic fluency.

signals.title: EPA grant backs community-driven workforce training in Southwest Virginia - Virginia Tech News
signals.signal_reading: EPA-funded community-driven workforce training in Southwest Virginia represents grassroots capacity-building that could enable distributed, deep skill development in an economically transitioning region—a counter-signal to concentration trends.

signals.title: Faculty mentorship fuels alumni impact in cybersecurity and artificial intelligence - Virginia Tech News
signals.signal_reading: Virginia Tech's cybersecurity and AI mentorship producing alumni impact reinforces New River Valley as a deep capability center, but the talent export pattern suggests knowledge concentration rather than regional distribution of expertise.
